_comment: br-frankenpandas-rc0923-epic-rust-parity-bugs-4qg5w.8 / DISC-025. FOUR fixtures,
named explicitly, because bulk regeneration is forbidden.
WHAT CHANGED IN THE ORACLE. op_series_str_encode asked pandas
`.str.encode('utf-8').str.len()` and op_series_str_decode returned its input
unchanged, both commented 'FP's str.encode reports the UTF-8 byte length' /
'FP's str.decode is the identity': the oracle answered FrankenPandas' question,
so these fixtures pinned DISC-025's divergence as if it were pandas' answer.
They now ask pandas `.str.encode('utf-8')` and `.str.decode('utf-8')`, and
scalar_to_json writes a bytes value as fp-types' bytes object cell
({"kind": "object", "value": {"bytes": [...]}}) instead of the text "b'..'".
WHY THIS IS NOT LAUNDERING FP'S ANSWER INTO THE CORPUS. The moved values are
pandas' own (live 2.2.3, below), and FrankenPandas changed in the same unit of
work to produce them: StringAccessor::encode returns bytes cells
(ObjectValue::Bytes, new) with a missing value kept and the name kept;
decode reads bytes and gives NaN for anything else. Against the OLD fp code
all four regenerated fixtures FAIL (lengths / identity) - the gate tightened.
INTEGRITY CHECK (the price of a gate change): rows admitted or moved = 4 (these
four; no other fixture carries series_str_encode / series_str_decode, and no
expected value anywhere in the corpus was a "b'" text the new bytes branch could
re-read). WIN/LOSE against the pre-change code: 0 WIN / 4 LOSE. Against this
commit's code: 4 WIN.
